members.statement_original:
Eq. (2) can be equivalently expressed in terms of a spectral component for an arbitrary norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb R^d$. More precisely, we obtain the weak convergence
\[
\mathcal L(u^{-1}X^*\mid\|X^*\|>u)\xrightarrow{w}\mathcal L(Y\Theta),\qquad u\to\infty,
\]
(5)
where $Y$ is a unit Pareto random variable and, independently from $Y$, $\Theta$ is a $[0,\infty)^d$-valued random vector satisfying $\|\Theta\|=1$ almost surely, i.e.
\[
\mathbb P(\Theta\in S^+_{d-1})=1,\qquad\text{where }S^+_{d-1}=\{x\in[0,\infty)^d:\|x\|=1\}.
\]
In the following, we will focus on the maximum norm $\|\cdot\|=\|\cdot\|_\infty$ which is not a serious restrictions as all norms on $\mathbb R^d$ are equivalent.
